According to Bloomberg, Apple is targeting the launch of an OLED-equipped iPad mini before October, and has shared its anticipated update timeline for the entry-level iPad, iPad Air, and iPad Pro. Details below.

"The biggest iPad mini revamp in half a decade"

While rumours of the next iPad mini featuring an OLED display have long circulated, with a launch expected later this year, Bloomberg has now provided a more precise release window.

According to the latest report, "Apple is preparing to release a new OLED iPad mini (codenamed J510) as early as this autumn, with plans to officially go on sale before October." The report also noted that Apple is "working on an OLED upgrade for the iPad Air," but "is not currently developing a base-model iPad with OLED, and will continue using the cheaper LCD technology for the foreseeable future."

Earlier this week, Weibo tipster yeux1122 also stated that the iPad mini would adopt an OLED display, but claimed the device would not feature ProMotion technology, with the refresh rate remaining fixed at 60Hz.

Returning to the Bloomberg report, the article points out that the addition of OLED technology could further drive up the price of the iPad mini. The device currently starts at US$599, higher than the US$499 price tag from just a few weeks ago, before Apple significantly raised prices across multiple product lines.

The report also shared Apple's anticipated timeline for the rest of the iPad lineup:

According to people familiar with the matter, a new entry-level iPad (codenamed J581) is expected to launch as early as the first quarter of next year. The main change will be a faster processor, rather than a major design overhaul. The new iPad Air will continue to be offered in both 11-inch and 13-inch versions. The new models (codenamed J807 and J837) are expected to arrive in spring. Apple also plans to release new iPad Pro models around the same time, which Bloomberg reported on earlier last month.

Finally, Bloomberg reiterated reports from several days ago, stating that Apple is expected to update the Apple Pencil next year, with the new model potentially adopting a replaceable battery design.
